headline: On a whole page of 400 tiles the ordering is set by two costs that have nothing to do with each other: per-render hashing, which puts `emotion` at 2.46 ms/1k, and class-attribute bytes, which put zero-runtime `bamboo` at 0.512 against `vanilla`'s 0.319.

microbench.why: The closest thing to a real page: 400 tiles mixing static, variant, dynamic and composed styling. `vanilla` and the css-prop fold lead at 0.319 and 0.331 ms/1k with nothing on the render path, `stylex-layers` at 0.348. `emotion` is 7.7× the leader at 2.46, with `@emotion/hash` (85.6 ms) and `@emotion/styled` (85.1 ms) splitting most of a 391 ms JS window, and `goober` and `styled-components` follow at 1.45 and 1.41. `bamboo` at 0.512 does no styling work at all, its own package costing 8.04 ms of a 97.2 ms window, and pays in react-dom instead (87.0 ms) writing 230 atomic class tokens across the two-tile snapshot where `vanilla` writes 28.

autocannon.why: A full page per request compresses the field: 249 req/s for the css-prop fold, 247 for `vanilla`, 223 for the styled fold. `bamboo` (117), `panda` (101) and the utility lanes (108-123) serve roughly half that, and the difference is response bytes. `emotion` at 69 req/s is the floor.

attribution.why: `vanilla` renders a tile in 2.10 ms and the css-prop fold in 2.25 with a 0.298 ms library slice. `emotion` spends 7.80 of its 13.6 ms inside its own packages and `goober` 5.99 of 8.70. `bamboo` and `panda` report a zero library slice and still cost 3.57 ms each, all of it React: 87.0 and 91.1 ms of react-dom in a JS window of about 98 ms, which is what long atomic class names cost when a page carries 400 of them.

hydrate.why: The static-sheet lanes hydrate at 59.6-64.9 ms with no style, layout or paint inside the span. `goober` (267 ms) and `styled-components` (258 ms) inject 400 tiles' worth of rules during hydration and record a 6.6-6.8 ms layout pass on top of 0.6-1.6 ms of recalc, the largest browser cost in any hydration span here, while `emotion` reaches 136 ms. The top of the fast cluster spans 2%, a tie.

inp.why: Toggling a wishlist re-renders one tile. The build-time lanes need 8.3-11.2 ms and under 1.2 ms of JS. `emotion` re-serializes the tile for 52.6 ms, `goober` 34.2 and `styled-components` 28.3, the only lanes where an interaction on a real page becomes visible. `panda` hoists its calls here and stays fast at 10.5 ms.

mount.why: Mounting 400 tiles costs 135-153 ms for every lane whose sheet is a file, `bamboo` (137 ms) and `panda` (140 ms) included. `emotion` (253 ms), `goober` (224 ms) and `styled-components` (220 ms) build the sheet before first paint. Inside the static-sheet group the top three sit within 1.5%.

renderTiming.why: Counts tie at one recalculation and one layout for every lane, so the ordering falls to the recalc's own cost, and that inverts the SSR result: `goober` (0.259 ms) and `styled-components` (0.273 ms) recalculate fastest because their sheets carry only the rules the page used, while `bamboo` (1.16 ms) and `cnfast` (0.956 ms) hand the selector matcher hundreds of atomic and utility classes per tile. No lane forces a synchronous layout.

payload.why: A real page is where payload separates: the css-prop fold ships 7.14 kB gzipped and `vanilla` 7.79. Atomic and utility naming roughly doubles that, `stylex-layers` 13.0 kB, `bamboo` 17.2 kB, `panda` 21.2 kB, `cnfast` 27.7 kB. `goober` at 11.2 kB is the cheapest runtime lane because it ships no sheet at all, only the code that builds one.

nsweep.why: Scaling the page to 4000 tiles holds `vanilla` at 18.0 ms and the css-prop fold at 18.7. `bamboo` (33.8 ms) and `panda` (34.3 ms) grow with the markup they emit per tile and `cnfast` reaches 27.7. `emotion` climbs to 140 ms and `goober` to 85.4, their per-render hash multiplied by 4000 tiles.
